exposure: cardiac disease (rheumatic heart lesions, congenital heart disease, mitral stenosis, atrial septal defect)
outcome: maternal complications (congestive cardiac failure, atrial fibrillation, supraventricular tachycardia, pregnancy-induced hypertension, severe anaemia, maternal mortality)
fetal complications (intrauterine growth restriction, preterm birth, perinatal deaths)
cohort: The study included 127 pregnant women with cardiac disease.
finding: Heart disease in pregnancy is a high-risk condition with a major impact on maternal and fetal outcomes.
mod_finding: Fifty-three percent of cases delivered vaginally, and 40% by caesarean section.
